71	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
72	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
73	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
74	
75	
76	def _normalize_job(job: object) -> tuple[str, int, int, list[str]]:
77	    if not isinstance(job, dict) or set(job.keys()) != _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
78	        raise ValueError("job must be an object with exactly job_id, deadline, "
79	                         "energy_wh and residency_regions")
80	
81	    job_id = job["job_id"]
82	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
83	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
84	
85	    deadline = job["deadline"]
86	    if not _is_plain_int(deadline) or deadline < 0:
87	        raise ValueError("deadline must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
88	
89	    energy_wh = job["energy_wh"]
90	    if not _is_plain_int(energy_wh) or energy_wh <= 0:
91	        raise ValueError("energy_wh must be a non-boolean positive integer")
92	
93	    regions = job["residency_regions"]
94	    if not isinstance(regions, list) or not regions:
95	        raise ValueError("residency_regions must be a non-empty list")
96	    normalized: list[str] = []
97	    seen: set[str] = set()
98	    for region in regions:
99	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
100	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
101	        if region in seen:
102	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
103	        seen.add(region)
104	        normalized.append(region)
105	    normalized.sort()  # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
106	
107	    return job_id, deadline, energy_wh, normalized
108	
109	
110	def _validate_regions(regions: object) -> list[str]:
111	    if not isinstance(regions, list) or not regions:
112	        raise ValueError("residency_regions must be a non-empty list")
113	    seen: set[str] = set()
114	    for region in regions:
115	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region or region in seen:
116	            raise ValueError("invalid residency region")
117	        seen.add(region)
118	    if regions != sorted(regions):
119	        raise ValueError("residency_regions are not normalized")
120	    return list(regions)
121	
122	
123	def _validate_structure(
124	    data: object,
125	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]:
126	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
127	        raise ValueError("registry root must be an object with keys "
128	                         "version, jobs and idempotency")
129	
130	    version = data["version"]
131	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
132	        raise ValueError("unsupported registry version")
133	
134	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
135	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
136	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict):
137	        raise ValueError("jobs and idempotency must be objects")
138	
139	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
140	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
141	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
142	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
143	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record.keys()) != set(_JOB_FIELDS):
144	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
145	        if record["job_id"] != name:
146	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
147	        if not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
148	            raise ValueError("job_id must be a string")
149	        if not _is_plain_int(record["deadline"]) or record["deadline"] < 0:
150	            raise ValueError("invalid deadline")
151	        if not _is_plain_int(record["energy_wh"]) or record["energy_wh"] <= 0:
152	            raise ValueError("invalid energy_wh")
153	        _validate_regions(record["residency_regions"])
154	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
155	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
156	        jobs[name] = dict(record)
157	
158	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
159	    referenced: set[str] = set()
160	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
161	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
162	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
163	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
164	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a registered job")
165	        if job_id in referenced:
166	            raise ValueError("job registered under more than one idempotency key")
167	        referenced.add(job_id)
168	        idempotency[key] = job_id
169	
170	    return jobs, idempotency

173	def _load(realpath: str) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]:
174	    try:
175	        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
176	            text = handle.read()
177	    except FileNotFoundError:
178	        return {}, {}
179	
180	    try:
181	        data = strict_loads(text)
182	    except ValueError as exc:
183	        raise ValueError(f"registry file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
184	    return _validate_structure(data)

186	
187	def _atomic_write(
188	    realpath: str,
189	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
190	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
191	) -> None:
192	    payload = {
193	        "version": _VERSION,
194	        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
195	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
196	    }
197	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
198	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
199	
200	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
201	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-", suffix=".tmp")
202	    try:
203	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
204	            handle.write(text)
205	            handle.flush()
206	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
207	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
208	    except BaseException:
209	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
210	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
211	        raise
212	
213	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
214	    try:
215	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
216	    finally:
217	        os.close(dir_fd)

220	def register(
221	    path: str,
222	    job: dict[str, object],
223	    idempotency_key: str,
224	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
225	    """Register a job idempotently, persisting it as compact UTF-8 JSON.
226	
227	    Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries job_id, deadline,
228	    energy_wh, residency_regions (sorted by code point) and ``state`` set to
229	    ``"queued"``; ``created`` is ``True`` for a new registration and ``False``
230	    when the idempotency key replays an identical, normalized job.
231	    """
232	    if not isinstance(path, str):
233	        raise ValueError("path must be a string")
234	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
235	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
236	    job_id, deadline, energy_wh, regions = _normalize_job(job)
237	
238	    store = _get_store(path)
239	    with store.lock:
240	        jobs, idempotency = _load(store.realpath)
241	        record: dict[str, object] = {
242	            "job_id": job_id,
243	            "deadline": deadline,
244	            "energy_wh": energy_wh,
245	            "residency_regions": regions,
246	            "state": _STATE,
247	        }
248	
249	        existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
250	        if existing_id is not None:
251	            existing = jobs[existing_id]
252	            if existing != record:
253	                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
254	                                 "different job")
255	            return dict(existing), False
256	
257	        if job_id in jobs:
258	            raise ValueError("job_id is already registered under another "
259	                             "idempotency key")
260	
261	        jobs[job_id] = record
262	        idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
263	        _atomic_write(store.realpath, jobs, idempotency)
264	        return dict(record), True
265	
266	
267	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
268	# Version 2: complete scheduling-constraint jobs
269	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
270	
271	
272	@contextlib.contextmanager
273	def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
274	    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
275	    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
276	    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
277	    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
278	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
279	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
280	    try:
281	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
282	        try:
283	            yield
284	        finally:
285	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
286	    finally:
287	        os.close(fd)
288	
289	
290	def _normalize_region_list(value: object, label: str) -> list[str]:
291	    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
292	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a non-empty list")
293	    normalized: list[str] = []
294	    seen: set[str] = set()
295	    for region in value:
296	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
297	            raise ValueError(f"{label} must be non-empty strings")
298	        if region in seen:
299	            raise ValueError(f"{label} must be distinct")
300	        seen.add(region)
301	        normalized.append(region)
302	    normalized.sort()  # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
303	    return normalized
304	
305	
306	def _normalize_submit_job(job: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
307	    if not isinstance(job, dict) or set(job.keys()) != _SUBMIT_REQUIRED_FIELDS:
308	        raise ValueError("job must be an object with exactly job_id, work, "
309	                         "deadline, regions, residency, max_cost and "
310	                         "carbon_cap")
311	
312	    job_id = job["job_id"]
313	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
314	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
315	
316	    work = job["work"]
317	    if not _is_plain_int(work) or work <= 0:
318	        raise ValueError("work must be a non-boolean positive integer")
319	
320	    for name in ("deadline", "max_cost", "carbon_cap"):
321	        value = job[name]
322	        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
323	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
324	                             "integer")
325	
326	    regions = _normalize_region_list(job["regions"], "regions")
327	    residency = _normalize_region_list(job["residency"], "residency")
328	    if not set(residency).issubset(regions):
329	        raise ValueError("residency regions must be a subset of regions")
330	
331	    return {
332	        "job_id": job_id,
333	        "work": work,
334	        "deadline": job["deadline"],
335	        "regions": regions,
336	        "residency": residency,
337	        "max_cost": job["max_cost"],
338	        "carbon_cap": job["carbon_cap"],
339	        "state": _STATE,
340	    }
341	
342	
343	def _validate_region_field(value: object, label: str) -> list[str]:
344	    normalized = _normalize_region_list(value, label)
345	    if value != normalized:
346	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be sorted by code point and free "
347	                         "of duplicates")
348	    return normalized

351	def _check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
352	    keys = list(mapping)
353	    if keys != sorted(keys):
354	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")
355	
356	
357	def _validate_submit_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
358	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str], dict[str, dict[str, str]]
359	]:
360	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_ROOT_FIELDS):
361	        raise ValueError("acceptance file root must be an object with keys "
362	                         "version, jobs, idempotency and audit")
363	
364	    version = data["version"]
365	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _SUBMIT_VERSION:
366	        raise ValueError("unsupported acceptance file version")
367	
368	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
369	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
370	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
371	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) \
372	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
373	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
374	        raise ValueError("jobs, idempotency and audit must be objects")
375	    _check_sorted_keys(jobs_raw, "jobs")
376	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
377	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
378	
379	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
380	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
381	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
382	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
383	        if not isinstance(record, dict) \
384	                or set(record.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS):
385	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
386	        if record["job_id"] != name or not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
387	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
388	        if not _is_plain_int(record["work"]) or record["work"] <= 0:
389	            raise ValueError("invalid work")
390	        for field in ("deadline", "max_cost", "carbon_cap"):
391	            if not _is_plain_int(record[field]) or record[field] < 0:
392	                raise ValueError(f"invalid {field}")
393	        regions = _validate_region_field(record["regions"], "regions")
394	        residency = _validate_region_field(record["residency"], "residency")
395	        if not set(residency).issubset(regions):
396	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be a subset of regions")
397	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
398	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
399	        jobs[name] = {field: record[field] for field in _SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS}
400	
401	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
402	    referenced: set[str] = set()
403	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
404	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
405	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
406	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
407	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference an accepted "
408	                             "job")
409	        if job_id in referenced:
410	            raise ValueError("job accepted under more than one idempotency "
411	                             "key")
412	        referenced.add(job_id)
413	        idempotency[key] = job_id
414	
415	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
416	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
417	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
418	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
419	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
420	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_EVENT_FIELDS):
421	            raise ValueError("submit audit event has invalid fields")
422	        event_key = event["key"]
423	        job_id = event["job_id"]
424	        result = event["result"]
425	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
426	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
427	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
428	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference an accepted job")
429	        if result != _STATE:
430	            raise ValueError("audit event result must be queued")
431	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "job_id": job_id,
432	                       "result": result}
433	
434	    # The three sections describe one acceptance history: each
435	    # idempotency key binds one job and one submit event, every accepted
436	    # job has both, and the event and the map agree on the job.
437	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
438	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
439	    for key, job_id in idempotency.items():
440	        if events[key]["job_id"] != job_id:
441	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
442	                             "entry")
443	    if set(jobs) != referenced:
444	        raise ValueError("every accepted job must be bound to an "
445	                         "idempotency key")
446	
447	    return jobs, idempotency, events
448	
449	
450	def _load_submit_file(
451	    realpath: str,
452	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str],
453	           dict[str, dict[str, str]], bytes | None]:
454	    try:
455	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
456	            raw = handle.read()
457	    except FileNotFoundError:
458	        return {}, {}, {}, None
459	
460	    try:
461	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
462	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
463	        raise ValueError(
464	            f"acceptance file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
465	    try:
466	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
467	        data = finite_loads(text)
468	    except ValueError as exc:
469	        raise ValueError(
470	            f"acceptance file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
471	    jobs, idempotency, events = _validate_submit_structure(data)
472	    return jobs, idempotency, events, raw

475	def _serialize_submit_file(
476	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
477	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
478	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
479	) -> bytes:
480	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
481	    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
482	    payload = {
483	        "version": _SUBMIT_VERSION,
484	        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
485	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
486	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
487	    }
488	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
489	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
490	    return text.encode("utf-8")

493	def _rollback_submit_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
494	                          old_bytes: bytes | None,
495	                          first: BaseException) -> None:
496	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
497	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
498	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
499	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
500	    try:
501	        if old_bytes is None:
502	            try:
503	                os.unlink(realpath)
504	            except FileNotFoundError:
505	                pass
506	        else:
507	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
508	                dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
509	            try:
510	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
511	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
512	                    handle.flush()
513	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
514	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
515	            except BaseException:
516	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
517	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
518	                raise
519	        _fsync_directory(directory)
520	    except OSError as recovery:
521	        raise recovery from first

524	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
525	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
526	    try:
527	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
528	    finally:
529	        os.close(dir_fd)

532	def _commit_submit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
533	                        old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
534	    # One durable commit for jobs, the idempotency map and the audit
535	    # event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
536	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
537	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful submit leaves the original file
538	    # byte-for-byte.
539	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
540	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
541	        dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-submit-", suffix=".tmp")
542	    try:
543	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
544	            handle.write(payload)
545	            handle.flush()
546	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
547	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
548	    except BaseException as first:
549	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
550	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
551	        raise
552	    try:
553	        _fsync_directory(directory)
554	    except BaseException as first:
555	        _rollback_submit_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
556	        raise

559	def submit(path: str, job: dict[str, object], idempotency_key: str
560	           ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
561	    """Persistently accept a complete scheduling-constraint job.
562	
563	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The job
564	    must be an object with exactly the seven top-level fields job_id,
565	    work, deadline, regions, residency, max_cost and carbon_cap: a
566	    non-empty id, a positive work amount, non-negative deadline,
567	    max_cost and carbon_cap (booleans rejected), and two non-empty lists
568	    of distinct non-empty region strings, residency a subset of regions.
569	    Any deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
570	
571	    A first acceptance saves the canonical job -- both region lists
572	    sorted by code point, state ``"queued"`` -- together with the
573	    idempotency binding and a submit audit event carrying the key, the
574	    job id and the queued result, all three in one durable commit, and
575	    returns ``(record, True)``. Replaying the same key with an
576	    equivalent job returns the stored record with ``False`` without
577	    adding an event or rewriting the file; the same key with a different
578	    job, an already accepted job id under another key, or any constraint
579	    mismatch raises ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
580	
581	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
582	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
583	    version, structure, ordering or references) raises ``ValueError``;
584	    any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Calls serialize
585	    across threads and processes per resolved real path.
586	    """
587	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
588	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
589	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
590	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
591	    record = _normalize_submit_job(job)
592	    job_id = record["job_id"]
593	
594	    store = _get_store(path)
595	    with store.lock:
596	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
597	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
598	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
599	            jobs, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_submit_file(
600	                store.realpath)
601	
602	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
603	            if existing_id is not None:
604	                existing = jobs[existing_id]
605	                if existing != record:
606	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
607	                                     "a different job")
608	                return dict(existing), False
609	
610	            if job_id in jobs:
611	                raise ValueError("job_id is already accepted under another "
612	                                 "idempotency key")
613	
614	            jobs[job_id] = record
615	            idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
616	            events[idempotency_key] = {
617	                "key": idempotency_key,
618	                "job_id": job_id,
619	                "result": _STATE,
620	            }
621	            _commit_submit_file(
622	                store.realpath,
623	                _serialize_submit_file(jobs, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
624	            return dict(record), True
625	
626	
627	def get(path: str, job_id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
628	    """Return a read-only copy of the accepted job stored under ``job_id``.
629	
630	    ``path`` and ``job_id`` must be non-empty strings, else
631	    ``ValueError``. A missing acceptance file raises
632	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including a version-1
633	    ``jobs.register`` file, which is never upgraded -- raises
634	    ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises ``KeyError(job_id)``; any
635	    other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. The call never
636	    writes, and the returned record is a fresh copy with job_id, work,
637	    deadline, regions, residency, max_cost, carbon_cap and state.
638	    """
639	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
640	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
641	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
642	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
643	
644	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
645	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
646	        jobs, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_submit_file(realpath)
647	    if raw is None:
648	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"acceptance file {realpath!r} does not exist")
649	    if job_id not in jobs:
650	        raise KeyError(job_id)
651	    return dict(jobs[job_id])

1	"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process resource-supply registry.
2	
3	One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
4	market:
5	
6	* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
7	  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
8	* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
9	* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
10	  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.
11	
12	Every read entry requires the on-disk document to be exactly the
13	canonical compact form :func:`_serialize` produces -- fields and keys
14	in their fixed/code-point order, no whitespace beyond structural
15	tokens, non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline. Any
16	out-of-order section, extra whitespace, ``\\uXXXX``-escaped non-ASCII
17	character, or missing or duplicated final newline is a ``ValueError``.
18	
19	:func:`publish` appends a new version under an idempotency key,
20	:func:`get` reads one resource record back by id and optional version,
21	and :func:`feasible` joins a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file with the
22	supply file under both shared locks to rank the resources that can
23	serve one accepted job at an evaluation moment. The supply file is
24	never rewritten by the read paths, and a version-1 ``jobs.register``
25	file is not a supply file.
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	import contextlib
31	import fcntl
32	import json
33	import os
34	import tempfile
35	import threading
36	from typing import Any, Iterator
37	
38	from . import jobs as _jobs
39	from ._jsonio import finite_loads
40	
41	__all__ = ["publish", "get", "feasible"]
42	
43	_VERSION = 1
44	_RESOURCE_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "region", "capacity", "start", "end",
45	                    "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
46	_RECORD_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version", "region", "capacity", "start",
47	                  "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
48	_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "history", "idempotency", "audit")
49	_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "resource_id", "version")
50	_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"

54	    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
55	        self.realpath = realpath
56	        self.lock = threading.Lock()

64	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)

73	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
74	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
75	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

78	@contextlib.contextmanager
79	def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
80	    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
81	    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
82	    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
83	    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
84	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
85	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
86	    try:
87	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
88	        try:
89	            yield
90	        finally:
91	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
92	    finally:
93	        os.close(fd)

96	def _check_values(resource: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
97	    region = resource["region"]
98	    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
99	        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
100	
101	    capacity = resource["capacity"]
102	    if not _is_plain_int(capacity) or capacity <= 0:
103	        raise ValueError("capacity must be a non-boolean positive integer")
104	
105	    for name in ("start", "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
106	        value = resource[name]
107	        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
108	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
109	                             "integer")

111	        raise ValueError("start must not be later than end")
112	
113	    residency = resource["residency"]
114	    if not isinstance(residency, list) or not residency:
115	        raise ValueError("residency must be a non-empty list")
116	    seen: set[str] = set()
117	    for entry in residency:
118	        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry:
119	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
120	        if entry in seen:
121	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
122	        seen.add(entry)
123	    # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
124	    if residency != sorted(residency):
125	        raise ValueError("residency regions must be sorted by code point")
126	    if region not in seen:
127	        raise ValueError("residency regions must contain the resource region")

162	def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
163	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
164	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
165	]:
166	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
167	        raise ValueError("supply file root must be an object with keys "
168	                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")

170	    version = data["version"]

172	        raise ValueError("unsupported supply file version")

174	    history_raw = data["history"]

181	    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
182	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
183	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
184	
185	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
186	    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
187	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
188	            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
189	        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
190	            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
191	                             "per resource")

193	        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):

207	                "resource_id": resource_id,
208	                "version": index,
209	                "region": record["region"],
210	                "capacity": record["capacity"],
211	                "start": record["start"],
212	                "end": record["end"],
213	                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
214	                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],

217	        history[resource_id] = records
218	
219	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
220	    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():

229	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}

254	    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version

261	                             "entry")

274	def _canonical_bytes(
275	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
276	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
277	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
278	) -> bytes:
279	    # The canonical wire form every reader accepts: compact UTF-8 JSON
280	    # with non-ASCII written through, sections in their fixed field order
281	    # and each section's primary keys in code-point order, terminated by
282	    # exactly one newline. The round trip also rejects duplicate keys
283	    # (json.loads keeps the last occurrence) and any escaping of
284	    # non-ASCII characters that json.dumps would write through.
285	    return _serialize(history, idempotency, events)

289	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
290	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
291	]:

305	        data = finite_loads(text)

310	    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
311	    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
312	    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline. Any
313	    # extra whitespace, escaped non-ASCII character, reordered field or
314	    # missing/duplicated final newline is a ValueError.
315	    if raw != _canonical_bytes(history, idempotency, events):

357	                os.unlink(realpath)
358	            except FileNotFoundError:
359	                pass
360	        else:
361	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
362	                dir=directory, prefix=".resources-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
363	            try:
364	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
365	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
366	                    handle.flush()
367	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
368	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
369	            except BaseException:
370	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
371	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
372	                raise
373	        _fsync_directory(directory)
374	    except OSError as recovery:
375	        raise recovery from first

378	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
379	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
380	    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
381	    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
382	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
383	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
384	    # byte-for-byte.
385	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
386	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
387	        dir=directory, prefix=".resources-", suffix=".tmp")
388	    try:
389	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
390	            handle.write(payload)
391	            handle.flush()
392	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
393	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
394	    except BaseException:
395	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
396	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
397	        raise
398	    try:
399	        _fsync_directory(directory)
400	    except BaseException as first:
401	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
402	        raise

405	def publish(
406	    path: str,
407	    resource: dict[str, object],
408	    idempotency_key: str,
409	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
410	    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.
411	
412	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
413	    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
414	    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
415	    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
416	    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
417	    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
418	    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
419	    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
420	    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
421	
422	    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
423	    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
424	    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
425	    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
426	    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
427	    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
428	    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
429	    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
430	    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
431	    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
432	    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
433	
434	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
435	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
436	    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
437	    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
438	    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
439	    """
440	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
441	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
442	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
443	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
444	    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
445	    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]
446	
447	    store = _get_store(path)
448	    with store.lock:
449	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
450	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
451	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
452	            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
453	                store.realpath)
454	
455	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
456	            if existing_id is not None:
457	                event = events[idempotency_key]
458	                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
459	                if {field: existing[field]
460	                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
461	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
462	                                     "a different resource")
463	                return dict(existing), False
464	
465	            versions = history.get(resource_id)
466	            if versions is None:
467	                versions = []
468	                history[resource_id] = versions
469	                version = 1
470	            else:
471	                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
472	                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
473	                                     "versions")
474	                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1
475	
476	            record: dict[str, Any] = {
477	                "resource_id": resource_id,
478	                "version": version,
479	                "region": normalized["region"],
480	                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
481	                "start": normalized["start"],
482	                "end": normalized["end"],
483	                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
484	                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
485	                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
486	            }
487	            versions.append(record)
488	            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
489	            events[idempotency_key] = {
490	                "key": idempotency_key,
491	                "resource_id": resource_id,
492	                "version": version,
493	            }
494	            _commit_file(store.realpath,
495	                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
496	            return dict(record), True

499	def get(
500	    path: str,
501	    resource_id: str,
502	    version: int | None = None,
503	) -> dict[str, object]:
504	    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.
505	
506	    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
507	    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
508	    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
509	    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
510	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
511	    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown resource id raises
512	    ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown version
513	    ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
514	    ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record is a
515	    fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start, end,
516	    unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
517	    """
518	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
519	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
520	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
521	        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
522	    if version is not None \
523	            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
524	        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")
525	
526	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
527	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
528	        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
529	    if raw is None:
530	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
531	    versions = history.get(resource_id)
532	    if versions is None:
533	        raise KeyError(resource_id)
534	    if version is None:
535	        return dict(versions[-1])
536	    if version > len(versions):
537	        raise KeyError(version)
538	    return dict(versions[version - 1])

540	def feasible(
541	    job_path: str,
542	    supply_path: str,
543	    job_id: str,
544	    at: int,
545	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
546	    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.
547	
548	    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
549	    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
550	    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
551	    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
552	    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
553	    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.
554	
555	    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
556	    an invalid file -- including a supply file outside canonical
557	    compact form -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
558	    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
559	    ``OSError``.
560	
561	    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
562	    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
563	    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
564	    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
565	    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
566	    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
567	    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
568	    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
569	    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
570	    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
571	    candidate the list is empty.
572	    """
573	    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
574	        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
575	    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
576	        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
577	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
578	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
579	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
580	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
581	
582	    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
583	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
584	    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
585	    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
586	    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
587	        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
588	            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))
589	
590	        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
591	            job_real)
592	        if job_raw is None:
593	            raise FileNotFoundError(
594	                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
595	        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
596	        if supply_raw is None:
597	            raise FileNotFoundError(
598	                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
599	
600	        job = accepted.get(job_id)
601	        if job is None:
602	            raise KeyError(job_id)
603	
604	        work = job["work"]
605	        regions = set(job["regions"])
606	        residency = set(job["residency"])
607	        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
608	        for records in history.values():
609	            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
610	            for record in records:
611	                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
612	                    active = record
613	            if active is None:
614	                continue
615	            if active["region"] not in regions:
616	                continue
617	            if active["capacity"] < work:
618	                continue
619	            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
620	                continue
621	            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
622	                continue
623	            total_cost = work * active["unit_cost"]
624	            total_carbon = work * active["carbon_intensity"]
625	            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
626	                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
627	                continue
628	            candidates.append({
629	                "resource": dict(active),
630	                "total_cost": total_cost,
631	                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
632	            })
633	
634	    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (entry["resource"]["carbon_intensity"],
635	                                       entry["resource"]["unit_cost"],
636	                                       entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
637	    return candidates

"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process resource-supply registry.

One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
market:

* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.

Every read entry requires the on-disk document to be exactly the
canonical compact form :func:`_serialize` produces -- fields and keys
in their fixed/code-point order, no whitespace beyond structural
tokens, non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline. Any
out-of-order section, extra whitespace, ``\\uXXXX``-escaped non-ASCII
character, or missing or duplicated final newline is a ``ValueError``.

:func:`publish` appends a new version under an idempotency key,
:func:`get` reads one resource record back by id and optional version,
and :func:`feasible` joins a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file with the
supply file under both shared locks to rank the resources that can
serve one accepted job at an evaluation moment. The supply file is
never rewritten by the read paths, and a version-1 ``jobs.register``
file is not a supply file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import fcntl
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Iterator

from . import jobs as _jobs
from ._jsonio import finite_loads

__all__ = ["publish", "get", "feasible"]

_VERSION = 1
_RESOURCE_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "region", "capacity", "start", "end",
                    "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
_RECORD_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version", "region", "capacity", "start",
                  "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity", "residency")
_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "history", "idempotency", "audit")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "resource_id", "version")
_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"


class _Store:
    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}


def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = _Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _check_values(resource: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    region = resource["region"]
    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")

    capacity = resource["capacity"]
    if not _is_plain_int(capacity) or capacity <= 0:
        raise ValueError("capacity must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    for name in ("start", "end", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
        value = resource[name]
        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
                             "integer")
    if resource["start"] > resource["end"]:
        raise ValueError("start must not be later than end")

    residency = resource["residency"]
    if not isinstance(residency, list) or not residency:
        raise ValueError("residency must be a non-empty list")
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for entry in residency:
        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry:
            raise ValueError("residency regions must be non-empty strings")
        if entry in seen:
            raise ValueError("residency regions must be distinct")
        seen.add(entry)
    # Python str ordering is Unicode code-point ordering.
    if residency != sorted(residency):
        raise ValueError("residency regions must be sorted by code point")
    if region not in seen:
        raise ValueError("residency regions must contain the resource region")


def _normalize_resource(resource: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_RESOURCE_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("resource must be an object with exactly "
                         "resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, "
                         "unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency")

    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")

    normalized: dict[str, Any] = {
        "resource_id": resource_id,
        "region": resource["region"],
        "capacity": resource["capacity"],
        "start": resource["start"],
        "end": resource["end"],
        "unit_cost": resource["unit_cost"],
        "carbon_intensity": resource["carbon_intensity"],
        "residency": resource["residency"],
    }
    _check_values(normalized)
    normalized["residency"] = list(normalized["residency"])
    return normalized


def _check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
    keys = list(mapping)
    if keys != sorted(keys):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")


def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("supply file root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported supply file version")

    history_raw = data["history"]
    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
    audit_raw = data["audit"]
    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")

    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
                             "per resource")
        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
                raise ValueError("resource record has invalid fields")
            if record["resource_id"] != resource_id:
                raise ValueError("resource record id does not match its key")
            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
                    or record["version"] != index:
                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
            _check_values(record)
            if records and record["start"] <= records[-1]["start"]:
                raise ValueError("resource starts must increase across "
                                 "versions")
            records.append({
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": index,
                "region": record["region"],
                "capacity": record["capacity"],
                "start": record["start"],
                "end": record["end"],
                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(record["residency"]),
            })
        history[resource_id] = records

    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
                or resource_id not in history:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
                             "resource")
        idempotency[key] = resource_id

    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("publish audit event has invalid fields")
        event_key = event["key"]
        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
        event_version = event["version"]
        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
                or resource_id not in history:
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
                             "resource")
        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
                or event_version > len(history[resource_id]):
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
                             "version")
        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "resource_id": resource_id,
                       "version": event_version}

    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
    # idempotency key binds one resource and one publish event, the map
    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version
    # is bound to exactly one event.
    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
    for key, resource_id in idempotency.items():
        if events[key]["resource_id"] != resource_id:
            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
                             "entry")
    published = {(resource_id, record["version"])
                 for resource_id, records in history.items()
                 for record in records}
    bound = {(event["resource_id"], event["version"])
             for event in events.values()}
    if bound != published:
        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
                         "audit event")

    return history, idempotency, events


def _canonical_bytes(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # The canonical wire form every reader accepts: compact UTF-8 JSON
    # with non-ASCII written through, sections in their fixed field order
    # and each section's primary keys in code-point order, terminated by
    # exactly one newline. The round trip also rejects duplicate keys
    # (json.loads keeps the last occurrence) and any escaping of
    # non-ASCII characters that json.dumps would write through.
    return _serialize(history, idempotency, events)


def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
]:
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return {}, {}, {}, None

    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
        data = finite_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    history, idempotency, events = _validate_structure(data)
    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline. Any
    # extra whitespace, escaped non-ASCII character, reordered field or
    # missing/duplicated final newline is a ValueError.
    if raw != _canonical_bytes(history, idempotency, events):
        raise ValueError(
            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
    return history, idempotency, events, raw


def _serialize(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
    # surfaces chained after the original error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".resources-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
    # byte-for-byte.
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".resources-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise


def publish(
    path: str,
    resource: dict[str, object],
    idempotency_key: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.

    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.

    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.

    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
                store.realpath)

            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
            if existing_id is not None:
                event = events[idempotency_key]
                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
                if {field: existing[field]
                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different resource")
                return dict(existing), False

            versions = history.get(resource_id)
            if versions is None:
                versions = []
                history[resource_id] = versions
                version = 1
            else:
                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
                                     "versions")
                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1

            record: dict[str, Any] = {
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
                "region": normalized["region"],
                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
                "start": normalized["start"],
                "end": normalized["end"],
                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
            }
            versions.append(record)
            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
            events[idempotency_key] = {
                "key": idempotency_key,
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
            }
            _commit_file(store.realpath,
                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
            return dict(record), True


def get(
    path: str,
    resource_id: str,
    version: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.

    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown resource id raises
    ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown version
    ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record is a
    fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start, end,
    unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
    if version is not None \
            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
    if raw is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
    versions = history.get(resource_id)
    if versions is None:
        raise KeyError(resource_id)
    if version is None:
        return dict(versions[-1])
    if version > len(versions):
        raise KeyError(version)
    return dict(versions[version - 1])

def feasible(
    job_path: str,
    supply_path: str,
    job_id: str,
    at: int,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.

    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.

    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
    an invalid file -- including a supply file outside canonical
    compact form -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
    ``OSError``.

    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
    candidate the list is empty.
    """
    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))

        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
            job_real)
        if job_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
        if supply_raw is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")

        job = accepted.get(job_id)
        if job is None:
            raise KeyError(job_id)

        work = job["work"]
        regions = set(job["regions"])
        residency = set(job["residency"])
        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for records in history.values():
            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
            for record in records:
                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
                    active = record
            if active is None:
                continue
            if active["region"] not in regions:
                continue
            if active["capacity"] < work:
                continue
            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
                continue
            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
                continue
            total_cost = work * active["unit_cost"]
            total_carbon = work * active["carbon_intensity"]
            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
                continue
            candidates.append({
                "resource": dict(active),
                "total_cost": total_cost,
                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
            })

    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (entry["resource"]["carbon_intensity"],
                                       entry["resource"]["unit_cost"],
                                       entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
    return candidates
